title: Ability to control brightness of current screen from the keyboard
line: Meta+Brightness Up/Down now change only the brightness of the current screen, while the plain brightness keys still change all screens.
explanation: The brightness keys go through ScreenBrightnessController::adjustBrightnessStep(), which always moves every display by the same amount, and powerdevil had no global shortcut that targets a single display. So with two monitors there was no way to change just one of them from the keyboard. The change adds a per-display step function to the controller and two new global shortcuts, "Increase/Decrease Brightness of Current Screen" (default Meta+Brightness Up/Down). They ask KWin for its active output (org.kde.KWin.activeOutputName, the screen under the pointer or with the focused window, following KWin's setting) and step only that display, showing the OSD for it alone.

commits.message:
daemon: add shortcuts to change the brightness of the current screen

The brightness keys always change every screen together, so there was no
way to set a single monitor from the keyboard. This adds Meta+Brightness
Up/Down shortcuts that only change the screen KWin reports as active.

BUG: 501497

media.caption: Power Management shortcuts on master: brightness shortcuts only exist for all screens together.
New shortcuts "Increase/Decrease Brightness of Current Screen", bound to Meta+Brightness Up/Down.
Master, pointer on the right screen: Brightness Down changes both screens (OSD lists both). Meta+Brightness Down does nothing.
With the fix, pointer on the right screen: Meta+Brightness Down changes only Virtual-1, and the OSD shows only that screen.
Master: after using the keyboard, both screens have moved together.
With the fix: right screen lowered to 90% and left screen to 80% separately, each with Meta+Brightness Down.
